items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I’d met Oliver Nelson when were playing with Frank Sinatra with Red Norvo. I’d met him in Atlantic City. He was playing with Wild Bill Davis.

ctx.x: And what were some of the things that maybe weren’t as exciting as performing with Count Basie that you do on a day-to-day basis to allow you to live in New York?

Well, jeez, that’s hard to say, to put that together. I could tell you a story about when I first moved here, I called Jerome Richardson, because he’d encouraged me to come, and he said, you know he was really encouraging, leaning on me really. And I’d met Oliver Nelson when were playing with Frank Sinatra with Red Norvo. I’d met him in Atlantic City. He was playing with Wild Bill Davis. Later he was playing with Basie for a short while when we were in Las Vegas. So Oliver said, “When you come to New York call…

of it was pretty interesting because there were a lot of big bands playing for singers. Even the pop music of the day, I mean we did dates with Quincy for Sarah Vaughan. And it was just a lot of fun. And the beauty and the exchange between the musicians and the fraternity of musicians was really great. It was just wonderful. I always felt that I was welcomed for whatever I could contribute, and I got the chance to learn from it. I’ve just never been able to reciprocate, you know, I have not. When young musicians…
